newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian stocks reach record high at open.
newsitem.headline: Australian stocks reach record high at open.

text.p: Australian shares made tentative steps back above the 2,500 level at the open on Wednesday, the market attempting to establish a convincing foothold in territory recaptured late on Tuesday afternoon.
The All Ordinaries index added 5.9 points to 2,507.6 at the open and peaked at 2,508.3 a little later, surpassing the previous record high of 2,506.5 reached on February 14, 1997.
"It took some heart from the U.S. at the start but it is coming off now," said a Sydney-based dealer, pointing to the petering out of the early rush and the subsequent profit-taking.
"National Australia Bank ran into some profit-taking but that was not unexpected given the way it ran ahead of the rest. I think we are set for a choppy day with probably not much in it by the end."

Investors finally took some profits from the market's recent outperformer, National Australia Bank. It slipped 15 cents to its intraday low of A$17.00 (US$13.02) before finding support. The rest of the leaders, though, were narrowly mixed with little clear direction.
Rises outnumbered falls by a ratio of about nine to four, while about 41 percent of stocks traded remained steady.
